It's applied to the accuracy/defence roll when the attack is cast, like armour bonuses are." Short, Medium and Long fuse ARE the Accurate, Rapid and Longrange stances, so the distance is the only new input; the factors are quarters, exact in binary, so the floored stage loses nothing. The distance each band reads is clamped to the outer bands, min(7, max(1, d)): the clamp is the game's, where the bands fall is each sub-row's to say. The factor scales the whole attack roll, on the second tweet's placement; https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Chinchompa_(weapon) instead glosses it as scaling the Ranged attack bonus ("+100 Ranged attack ... long fuse ... effectively becomes +50"), which is a different number once the +64 constant is in the roll, and which no recorded assertion can distinguish. Unresolved pending in-game testing at a fixed Ranged bonus against a known Defence. Not modelled: the shared accuracy roll and the 3x3 splash, which are MultiTargetSplash's.

description: https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Twisted_bow accuracy percent = 140 + (3M-10)/100 - ((3M/10 - 100)^2)/100 clamped to [0, 140]; damage percent = 250 + (3M-14)/100 - ((3M/10 - 140)^2)/100 clamped to [0, 250]; every division truncated. M = max(target Magic level, Magic attack bonus) capped at 250, or 350 in CoX, which raises only the M input cap (the damage clamp never binds under it). Accuracy is its own late, separately-floored stage; damage folds into the main product with the other Ranged bonuses. Unsourced: below Magic level 4 the additive term's numerator is negative, where truncation and flooring differ (40% accuracy and 54% damage at Magic 1, against 39% and 53%); the wiki's markup carries no floor brackets and no statement of the direction, so this follows the truncation the rest of the formula uses.

accuracy.factor: clamp(140 + idiv(3 * min(player.inCoX ? 350 : 250, max(monster.magicLevel, monster.magicAttackBonus)) - 10, 100) - idiv(pow(idiv(3 * min(player.inCoX ? 350 : 250, max(monster.magicLevel, monster.magicAttackBonus)), 10) - 100, 2), 100), 0, 140) / 100

damage.factor: clamp(250 + idiv(3 * min(player.inCoX ? 350 : 250, max(monster.magicLevel, monster.magicAttackBonus)) - 14, 100) - idiv(pow(idiv(3 * min(player.inCoX ? 350 : 250, max(monster.magicLevel, monster.magicAttackBonus)), 10) - 140, 2), 100), 0, 250) / 100

All-fail: ~2/3 chance of 2, ~1/3 of 0. Always-max-hit targets are modelled as one certain hitsplat of the cascade's ceiling, pinned by the authored always-max-hit spec vectors. https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Halberd "the only melee weapons capable of hitting enemies" at a two-tile range: Sweep lands a second hitsplat against targets larger than 1x1, the second swing reducing the attack roll by 25% at roll level before hit chance is re-derived; folding it into the accuracy sum keeps (a1 + a2) * E exactly. https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Dragon_halberd says only "an additional second hit onto them, although with 25% reduced accuracy", which does not distinguish a 3/4 attack roll from a 3/4 hit chance: the roll-level reading is a pinned assumption whose only support is agreement with the reference battery. The damage bonus is already in maxHit.

Blood Forfeit "overrides the projectile's damage", so a proc shot pays the proc instead of the ordinary hit and the addend is the difference of expectations. https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Gemstone_Crab "Ruby bolt (e) special attacks treat the boss as if it has 300 Hitpoints and deal 60 damage, increased to 66 if using a Zaryte crossbow" - no decay to average.
